body.objective: Students will be able to build trust and focus with ensemble games.
body.iCan: I can build trust and focus with ensemble games.
successCriteria: I can concentrate and stay focused in a group activity
I can work safely and respectfully with others
I can explain why trust matters in drama
body.hook: On stage, actors have to trust each other completely. If your scene partner forgets a line, you need to catch them. If someone falls in a scene, you need to know the group has their back. Drama starts not with acting, but with trust and focus.

study.title: Building the Ensemble
study.question: How do trust and focus help a group create drama?
study.passage:
Ground rules: respect, safety, no touching without consent and instruction, and "pass" is always an option.
Warm-up, Pass the clap (5 minutes): In a circle, pass a clap from person to person, making eye contact. Then speed up, reverse direction, and send two claps at once.
Game 1, Count to 20 (5 minutes): The group counts to 20 one person at a time, with no set order. If two people speak at once, start again. Eyes closed for the second round.
Game 2, Mirror (8 minutes): In pairs, one leads slow movements and the other mirrors exactly. Switch leaders. Then try with no leader, both following each other.
Game 3, Guided walk (10 minutes): One partner closes their eyes (or uses a blindfold if comfortable). The other guides them around the room with gentle verbal directions only. Switch. Side-coaching: "Guides, keep your partner safe. Walkers, notice how it feels to trust."
Debrief circle (5 minutes): How did it feel to trust? What helped? Where did focus slip?

examples.title: Focus
examples.problem: How do you stay focused in Count to 20?
examples.answer: Listen to the group and wait for a gap

examples.title: Mirroring
examples.problem: How can a leader make mirroring easier?
examples.answer: Slow, smooth movements with eye contact

examples.title: Trust
examples.problem: What should a good guide do?
examples.answer: Speak clearly and calmly and steer away from obstacles
examples.explore: How did trust grow over the walk?

examples.title: Respect
examples.answer: People can step back if they aren't comfortable, which builds trust
examples.explore: How can the group support someone who passes?

practice.a: Focused actors draw the audience's attention to the story.

practice.q: Why might eyes closed make Count to 20 harder?
practice.a: You can't see cues, so you must listen more closely.

practice.q: How could an ensemble rebuild trust after a mistake?
practice.a: Talk it through, encourage each other and try again.
